chapter_name: Viram Chihnon Ka Sahi Upyog (Correct Use of Punctuation Marks)
learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will discover the traffic signals of writing that tell your readers exactly when to pause, stop, question, or show excitement!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🛑 What are Viram Chihn? (The Reading Traffic Lights)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: When we speak, we naturally pause, change our tone, or show emotion. How do we show this in writing? Using Viram Chihn (Punctuation)! Without them, writing becomes a confusing, breathless run-on sentence. Example: 'रुको मत जाने दो' (Stop don't let go) means the exact opposite of 'रुको मत, जाने दो' (Don't stop, let go)!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🏁 Purn Viram vs. ⏳ Alpviram (The Big Stop vs. Quick Breath)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The 'Purn Viram' (।) is the Hindi full stop. It acts as a red light, marking the absolute end of a sentence. The 'Alpviram' (,) is a comma. It acts as a yield sign, telling you to take a tiny breath when listing items or separating short phrases. Example: 'मैंने सेब, केला, और आम खाए।'

Put a '?' at the end of any sentence that asks a question (क्या, कौन, कहाँ). Put a '!' (Vismayadibodhak / Exclamation mark) after words that show sudden shock, joy, or sadness. Example: 'वाह! तुमने तो कमाल कर दिया।' (Wow! You did an amazing job.)

A 'Yojak' (-) is a short hyphen used to connect paired words (like माता-पिता, दिन-रात). A 'Nirdeshak' (—) is a slightly longer dash. It is used before giving examples, writing dialogues, or giving a list (like: 'निम्नलिखित बातों का ध्यान रखें—').

Quotation marks come in two styles! Single (' ') are used for highlighting special words, book titles, or pen names (like सूर्यकांत त्रिपाठी 'निराला'). Double (" ") are used to quote exactly what someone said, word for word! Example: नेताजी ने कहा, "तुम मुझे खून दो, मैं तुम्हें आजादी दूँगा।"

fun_activity.title: 🚦 The 'No Brakes' Paragraph Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Read this out loud in one breath: 'रोको मत जाने दो चोर भाग रहा है पुलिस कहाँ है जल्दी आओ'. Hard, right? Now, rewrite this sentence and add at least one Alpviram (,), one Purn Viram (।), one Prashnasoochak (?), and one Vismayadibodhak (!) to make it make sense!

quick_recap: ⭐ Viram Chihn are symbols used in writing to represent pauses and tone, ensuring clarity of meaning.
⭐ Purn Viram (।) marks the end of a sentence. Alpviram (,) is a short pause for listing items.
⭐ Prashnasoochak (?) is for questions, and Vismayadibodhak (!) is for strong emotions.
⭐ Yojak (-) connects paired words, while Nirdeshak (—) introduces lists or dialogues.
⭐ Uddharan Chihn (" ") are used to quote direct speech or highlight specific titles/words.
